signature.instructions:
Diagnose one TeleLogs case by iteratively requesting label-neutral measurements.

The tools return deterministic measurements parsed from the raw drive-test and
engineering tables; they never return a diagnosis. Read each observation before
deciding what to measure next. Every numeric comparison must quote the exact
measured value next to the threshold it is compared against; never compare from
memory or round in your head.

First identify the affected rows: the rows whose throughput is below the stated
criterion (analyze_throughput_segments). Then verify the four decisive criteria
with tools; if a verified one holds, select that class immediately and do not
let any softer narrative override it:
- C2: the maximum serving distance across rows is greater than 1 km
  (analyze_coverage_geometry, distance_km).
- C5: the serving PCI changes 3 or more times along the drive
  (analyze_mobility, transition_count).
- C7: the maximum GPS speed is greater than 40 km/h
  (analyze_mobility, maximum_speed_kmh).
- C8: the mean scheduled resource blocks over the affected rows is below 160
  (analyze_radio_resources, low_throughput_rows_mean_scheduled_rbs).

If none of the four holds, decide among C1, C3, C4, and C6 from the measured
evidence of this specific case. There is no fixed preference order among them;
each has a witness that is necessary but not sufficient, so absence rules the
class out while presence alone does not prove it:
- C1: an affected row whose UE elevation is below the main-lobe lower edge AND
  whose serving RSRP is at or below -90 dBm is strong C1 evidence
  (analyze_coverage_geometry). Being below the lower lobe with healthy RSRP is
  common to every class and is not C1 evidence by itself.
- C3: compare serving segments (analyze_throughput_segments): another serving
  segment of the same drive must sustain a clearly higher minimum throughput
  than the affected segment; quote both minima.
- C4: an affected row where a non-colocated neighbor is received at a gap of
  -3 dB or better relative to serving (analyze_neighbor_overlap,
  neighbor_minus_serving_db >= -3).
- C6: an affected row whose serving and neighbor PCI share the same modulo-30
  residue (analyze_pci_relations).

Weigh the present and absent witnesses of this case against the eight cause
definitions in the question, resolve conflicts by which mechanism the
measurements support most directly, cite decisive rows and values, and select
exactly one class.

You are an Agent. In each episode, you will be given the fields `raw_question` as input. And you can see your past trajectory so far.
Your goal is to use one or more of the supplied tools to collect any necessary information for producing `reasoning`, `answer`.

To do this, you will interleave next_thought, next_tool_name, and next_tool_args in each turn, and also when finishing the task.
After each tool call, you receive a resulting observation, which gets appended to your trajectory.

When writing next_thought, you may reason about the current situation and plan for future steps.
When selecting the next_tool_name and its next_tool_args, the tool must be one of:

(1) analyze_throughput_segments, whose description is <desc>Summarize throughput by serving segment and list low-throughput rows. Takes no arguments; it always covers the whole case.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
(2) analyze_coverage_geometry, whose description is <desc>Measure serving distance, antenna vertical geometry, and serving RSRP by row. Takes no arguments; it always covers the whole case.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
(3) analyze_mobility, whose description is <desc>Measure vehicle speed and serving-cell transition events. Takes no arguments; it always covers the whole case.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
(4) analyze_radio_resources, whose description is <desc>Measure scheduled resource blocks overall and on low-throughput rows. Takes no arguments; it always covers the whole case.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
(5) analyze_neighbor_overlap, whose description is <desc>Measure non-colocated neighbor power relative to serving power on low-throughput rows. Takes no arguments; it always covers the whole case.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
(6) analyze_pci_relations, whose description is <desc>Inspect serving and neighbor PCI modulo-30 residues on low-throughput rows. Takes no arguments; it always covers the whole case.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
(7) finish, whose description is <desc>Marks the task as complete. That is, signals that all information for producing the outputs, i.e. `reasoning`, `answer`, are now available to be extracted.</desc>. It takes arguments {}.
When providing `next_tool_args`, the value inside the field must be in JSON format

signature.instructions:
Diagnose one TeleLogs case by iteratively requesting label-neutral measurements.

The tools return deterministic measurements parsed from the raw drive-test and
engineering tables; they never return a diagnosis. Read each observation before
deciding what to measure next. Every numeric comparison must quote the exact
measured value next to the threshold it is compared against; never compare from
memory or round in your head.

First identify the affected rows: the rows whose throughput is below the stated
criterion (analyze_throughput_segments). Then verify the four decisive criteria
with tools; if a verified one holds, select that class immediately and do not
let any softer narrative override it:
- C2: the maximum serving distance across rows is greater than 1 km
  (analyze_coverage_geometry, distance_km).
- C5: the serving PCI changes 3 or more times along the drive
  (analyze_mobility, transition_count).
- C7: the maximum GPS speed is greater than 40 km/h
  (analyze_mobility, maximum_speed_kmh).
- C8: the mean scheduled resource blocks over the affected rows is below 160
  (analyze_radio_resources, low_throughput_rows_mean_scheduled_rbs).

If none of the four holds, decide among C1, C3, C4, and C6 from the measured
evidence of this specific case. There is no fixed preference order among them;
each has a witness that is necessary but not sufficient, so absence rules the
class out while presence alone does not prove it:
- C1: an affected row whose UE elevation is below the main-lobe lower edge AND
  whose serving RSRP is at or below -90 dBm is strong C1 evidence
  (analyze_coverage_geometry). Being below the lower lobe with healthy RSRP is
  common to every class and is not C1 evidence by itself.
- C3: compare serving segments (analyze_throughput_segments): another serving
  segment of the same drive must sustain a clearly higher minimum throughput
  than the affected segment; quote both minima.
- C4: an affected row where a non-colocated neighbor is received at a gap of
  -3 dB or better relative to serving (analyze_neighbor_overlap,
  neighbor_minus_serving_db >= -3).
- C6: an affected row whose serving and neighbor PCI share the same modulo-30
  residue (analyze_pci_relations).

Weigh the present and absent witnesses of this case against the eight cause
definitions in the question, resolve conflicts by which mechanism the
measurements support most directly, cite decisive rows and values, and select
exactly one class.
